title: Facilities strategic plan and elected Regional Chair
subtitle: Committee also received consent items, including a salt tender and transit hub pre-construction award, then met in closed session.
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended that staff explore a Facilities Strategic Plan {{vote:m2}}. It would cover an inventory of corporate facilities, operating costs, a five- to ten-year capital outlook, accommodation standards and options to consolidate or repurpose space. Staff would report back to Council on findings and next steps. Staff said they would first return with a report defining scope and financial impact, and estimated the work at 6-12 months.

The committee also recommended that Council ask the Province to support the continued election of the Regional Chair, either by voters or by Regional Council, to avoid a provincially appointed chair, and to consult the Region and area municipalities before changing regional governance {{vote:m3}}. The motion was amended during the meeting to add the Council-appointment option.

The committee approved the consent agenda {{vote:m1}}, which included a quarterly summary of tenders and quotations. It then met in closed session on labour and employee relations matters and negotiations, and adjourned. The next meeting is March 10.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Facilities staff explore a strategic plan covering inventory, operating costs, a capital outlook, accommodation standards and optimization options, and report back to Council.

The committee recommended that Council ask the Province to support a Regional Chair elected by voters or appointed by Regional Council, avoid legislating a provincial appointee, and consult the Region first.
The committee received the consent items for information and approved them, with item 6.1.1 (the quarterly tenders and quotations summary) removed for separate discussion.

debate: On the facilities plan, staff said the scope should also include demand for space, such as accommodation standards and work policies, not only what the Region owns. Staff gave a rough consultant cost range and a 6-12 month timeline.

Several councillors asked how the plan differs from the existing asset management plan. Staff said asset management covers building condition and servicing, while this plan covers how space is used, and that the two work better as separate plans.
One councillor raised timing, noting 2027 budget work would follow the election, and asked for a report to inform that budget. Staff proposed returning with a report on scope, options and resources.

On the Regional Chair motion, supporters said it defends local democracy and that the Province should be told in advance. Some said they would support it with reluctance, citing the Province's unpredictable response and the unresolved governance reform.

Opponents and undecided councillors called the motion premature, since no provincial proposal exists, and said the Province will act regardless. Others noted that many municipalities appoint chairs from among councillors. The mover said either election or Council appointment was acceptable, and the wording was amended.
